title_en: On Breaks in the Customary Order
body_ar:
ما يظهر من الخوارق على يد الولي وما يظهر على يد الساحر ما الفرق بينهما؟

أن أهل العلم ذكروا أن خوارق العادات سبعة أقسام، أربع منها للخير وثلاث للشر، فالأربع التي للخير هي أولا الإرهاصات التي تظهر عند ميلاد الأنبياء وفي صباهم كتصدع إيوان كسرى وخمود نار الفرس وما شاهدته حليمة من الخوارق في صبا النبي (ص) وشق صدره ونحوه فهذه أمور ليست من المعجزات ولكنها من الإرهاصات فهي تدل على بعثته، فهو إذ ذاك لم يبعث بعد، وإنما بعث على رأس أربعين سنة،

والنوع الثاني هو المعجزات، وهي ما يظهر على يد الأنبياء عند التحدي عند تبليغ رسالات ربهم، كنزول الوحي، وكالمعراج والإسراء وشق القمر ونحو ذلك وكناقة صالح وعصا موسى فهذا هو المعجزة وهي مختصة بالأنبياء،

القسم الثالث ما يسمى بكرامات الأولياء، وهو ما يكرم الله به من كان من أهل الطاعة والتقوى والإيمان مما يعينه على الطاعة، كقوة البدن بحيث يستطيع الإنسان الدوام على الوضوء والغسل، فهذا كرامة يكرم الله بها أولياءه، ومثل ذلك الحفاظ على الصف الأول أو على إجابة المنادي أو على الصلاة في الجماعة أو على ختم القرآن في كل يوم وليلة مثلا أو الحفاظ على قيام الليل في طيلة السنة، فهذا كرامة يكرم الله بها من شاء من أوليائه وهي خارقة لعادة جمهور الناس، فهذا النوع يسمى الكرامات، وأغلبها لا يتجه إلى الدنيا إنما يتجه إلى أمور الآخرة، فالكرامات في أغلبها لا تتجه إلى أمور الدنيا كأن يجد الإنسان نقودا أو سيارة أو هاتفا أو نحو ذلك فهذه أمور دنيوية تافهة وإكرام الله تعالى للعباد يتعلق بأمور أكبر من هذا كإكرامه لأوليائه بما يعينهم على عبادته وطاعته وما يزيدهم إيمانا وخشية وتقوى،

النوع الرابع هو ما يسمى بالعون، وهو ما يناله أواسط المسلمين ممن ليس مشهورا بالطاعة ولا بالعبادة فيقيض الله له أمرا خارقا للعادة بسبب إيمانه، كمن نفرت منه راحلته بخلاء من الأرض فأمسكتها عليه شجرة، فهذا النوع مما يعين على أمور الدنيا ليس داخلا في نطاق الكرامة ولكنه من العون يعين الله بها عباده، فيقيض لهم ما يعينهم على أمور دنياهم مما هو خارق للعادة،

هذه الأربع للخير أما الثلاث التي للشر فهي أولا ما يسمى بالإهانة، وهو ما يظهر من الخوارق على يد مدعي الرسالة الكاذب على خلاف دعواه، فمسيلمة الكذاب سمع أن النبي (ص) مسح على رأس صبي فلم يشب، بقي شعره أسود إلى أن مات وهو شيخ كبير، فمسح هو على رأس صبي فقرع، وسمع أن النبي (ص) بصق في بير كانت ملحا فصارت عذبا، فبصق هو في بير فيبست، فهذا النوع يسمى إهانة هو خارق للعادة فعلا، هذا خارق للعادة لكنه إهانة لأنه ليس على الوجه المطلوب وهو خلاف الوجه الذي يطلبه الإنسان،

النوع الثاني من هذه الخوارق التي هي للشر السحر، والسحر هو ما سبق تعريفه بقسميه، ما كان منه تخييلا وما كان تأثيرا، فهذا يحصل به خرق للعادة وهو للشر فهو كفر بصاحبه،

والنوع الثالث من الخوارق التي هي للشر ما كان مما يسمى بالكهانة ومخالطة الجن، فالجن يخرقون العادة للإنسان فيسمعون الكلمة الواحدة من الغيب فيضيفون إليها تسعا وتسعين كذبة، فيأتونه بمائة كلمة فيها كلمة واحدة صدق وتسعة وتسعون كذبة، فيخبر هو بما أخبروه به، فتارة يأتيه صادق وتارة يأتيه كاذب، كما قال صاف بن صياد لرسول الله (ص) عندما سأله كما في الصحيح، قال: ماذا يأتيك يا صاف؟ قال: يأتيني صادق وكاذب، قال: اخسأ فلن تعدو قدرك، فعرف النبي (ص) أنما يأتيه هو من الشيطان لأن ما كان من عند الله لا يكون فيه كاذب، لا بد أن يكون صادقا، فقال: يأتيني صادق وكاذب فقال: اخسأ فلن تعدو قدرك،

فإذن هذه هي خوارق العادة وأقسامها واضحة والتمييز بينها بين، وإنما يشكل على بعض الناس ما يحصل لبعض الأولياء من الإخبار ببعض المغيبات وهم أهل استقامة وصلاح وتارة يصدقون في ذلك وتارة يكذبون، والجواب عن هذا أنه يجب عليهم أن لا يخبروا بما اطلعوا عليه من ذلك، ويحرم عليهم الإخبار به، وإذا أخبروا ببعضه فكان صادقا فعلى أهل الإيمان أن لا يغتروا به وأن يعلموا أن هذا يحصل للصالح والطالح ويحصل للمؤمن وغيره،

ولذلك سئل الإمام الجنيد رحمه الله فقيل له: الولي هو الذي يطير في الهواء؟ قال: الغراب يطير في الهواء وينقر الدبر، قيل له: أهو الذي يمشي على الماء؟ قال: الحوت يمشي على الماء وتؤكل ميتته، قيل: أهو الذي يجمع بين المشرق والمغرب في آن واحد؟ قال: إبليس يجمع بين المشرق والمغرب في آن واحد وهو أخس خلق الله، قيل: فما الولي إذن؟ قال: من استقام حاله على وفق ما جاء به رسول الله (ص) من عند الله تعالى فهذا هو الولي وهذه هي الولاية التي يحرص عليها هي ولاية الله.
body_en:
What appears of extraordinary events at the hand of the friend of God, and what appears at the hand of the sorcerer — what is the difference between them?

The scholars have mentioned that breaks in the customary order are of seven kinds: four of them for good and three of them for evil.

The four that are for good are, first, the precursors (irhāṣāt) that appear at the birth of the prophets and in their childhood — such as the cracking of the arch of Chosroes, the dying down of the fire of the Persians, what Halimah witnessed of extraordinary things in the childhood of the Prophet, upon whom be peace, the opening of his breast, and the like. These are not miracles (muʿjizāt) but precursors; they point to his being sent, since at that time he had not yet been sent — he was sent at the completion of forty years.

The second kind is the miracles: what appears at the hand of the prophets at the point of challenge, in conveying the messages of their Lord — such as the descent of revelation, the Ascension and the Night Journey, the splitting of the moon and the like, and such as the she-camel of Salih and the staff of Moses. This is the miracle, and it belongs to the prophets alone.

The third kind is what is called the charisms of the friends of God (karāmāt al-awliyāʾ): what God honours with it whoever is of the people of obedience, God-consciousness (taqwā) and faith, from among the things that help him toward obedience — such as bodily strength, so that a person is able to keep up ablution and full washing; this is a charism with which God honours His friends. Of the same kind is keeping to the first row, or to answering the one who calls to prayer, or to praying in congregation, or to completing the Qur'an every day and night, for example, or keeping to the night prayer through the whole year. This is a charism with which God honours whom He wills of His friends, and it is a break with the custom of most people. This kind is called the charisms, and most of them are not directed toward this world but toward the affairs of the Hereafter. Charisms are in most cases not directed toward worldly matters, such as a person finding money or a car or a telephone or the like; those are trivial worldly matters, whereas God's honouring of His servants is bound up with matters greater than this — as when He honours His friends with what helps them toward His worship and His obedience, and with what increases them in faith, awe and God-consciousness.

The fourth kind is what is called assistance (ʿawn): what is attained by the middling sort of Muslims, who are not renowned for obedience or for worship, so that God ordains for such a person something that breaks the customary order on account of his faith — like one whose mount bolted from him in an empty tract of land and a tree held it back for him. This kind is among what gives help in worldly matters; it does not fall within the scope of the charism, but is of the assistance by which God assists His servants, ordaining for them what helps them in their worldly affairs, of what breaks the customary order.

These are the four for good. As for the three that are for evil: the first is what is called humiliation (ihānah), namely the extraordinary events that appear at the hand of a false claimant to messengerhood, contrary to his claim. Musaylimah the Liar heard that the Prophet, upon whom be peace, had wiped the head of a boy and that the boy did not go grey — his hair stayed black until he died an old man. So Musaylimah wiped the head of a boy, and the boy went bald. And he heard that the Prophet, upon whom be peace, spat into a well that was salt and it became sweet; so he spat into a well and it dried up. This kind is called humiliation: it is in fact a break in the customary order — this is a break in the customary order, but it is a humiliation, because it is not in the manner sought, and is the opposite of the manner the person seeks.

The second kind of these breaks that are for evil is sorcery (siḥr). Sorcery is what has already been defined, in its two kinds: what is illusion, and what is actual effect. By it a break in the customary order comes about, and it is for evil; it is unbelief on the part of the one who does it.

The third kind of the breaks that are for evil is what is called soothsaying (kihānah) and consorting with the jinn. The jinn break the customary order for the human being: they hear a single word from the unseen and add to it ninety-nine lies, so they bring him a hundred words, among which is one word of truth and ninety-nine lies. Then he reports what they have reported to him, so that at one time a truthful one comes to him and at another a lying one — as Saf ibn Sayyad said to the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, when he asked him, as is in the Ṣaḥīḥ. He said: 'What comes to you, Saf?' He said: 'A truthful one and a lying one come to me.' He said: 'Be off with you; you will never go beyond your measure.' So the Prophet, upon whom be peace, knew that what comes to him is from Satan, because what is from God has no liar in it — it must be truthful. So he said, 'A truthful one and a lying one come to me', and he said: 'Be off with you; you will never go beyond your measure.'

These, then, are the breaks in the customary order. Their divisions are clear and the distinction between them is plain. What causes difficulty for some people is only what happens to some of the friends of God: that they report certain things of the unseen, being people of uprightness and righteousness, and at times they are right in that and at times they are wrong. The answer to this is that they are obliged not to report what they have come upon of that; it is forbidden (ḥarām) for them to report it. And if they do report some of it and it turns out true, the people of faith must not be taken in by it, and must know that this happens to the righteous and to the corrupt, and happens to the believer and to others.

That is why Imam al-Junayd, may God have mercy on him, was asked. It was said to him: 'Is the friend of God the one who flies through the air?' He said: 'The crow flies through the air and pecks at sores.' It was said to him: 'Is he the one who walks on water?' He said: 'The fish walks on water, and its carrion is eaten.' It was said: 'Is he the one who joins east and west in a single moment?' He said: 'Iblis joins east and west in a single moment, and he is the basest of God's creation.' It was said: 'What, then, is the friend of God?' He said: 'One whose state is upright in accordance with what the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, brought from God, exalted.' This is the friend of God, and this is the friendship to be striven for: the friendship of God.

flags.context: أن أهل العلم ذكروا أن خوارق العادات سبعة أقسام
flags.note: The phrase is the organising term of the whole answer and recurs a dozen times. 'Miracle' must be avoided for it, because the Sheikh reserves المعجزة (miracle) for one of the seven kinds only. Whichever phrase is fixed must be used throughout the corpus.

flags.arabic: الغراب يطير في الهواء وينقر الدبر
flags.context: al-Junayd's answer to 'is the friend of God the one who flies in the air?'
options: the crow flies through the air and pecks at sores
the crow flies through the air and pecks at the galls on camels' backs
the crow flies through the air and pecks at dung
flags.note: الدَّبَر is a saddle sore on a camel's back; الدُّبُر would be something else entirely, and other transmissions of this saying of al-Junayd read العذرة, 'excrement'. The source is unvowelled. The point of the retort survives under all three readings — the crow does something base while flying — but the image differs, so a reviewer should fix the reading.

flags.context: كما قال صاف بن صياد لرسول الله (ص) عندما سأله كما في الصحيح، قال: ماذا يأتيك يا صاف؟
options: Saf ibn Sayyad, as the source names him
Ibn Sayyad (Ibn Sa'id), the boy of Medina of the Dajjal reports
flags.note: The source gives the name as صاف بن صياد and has the Prophet address him as 'yā Ṣāf'. The figure is the Ibn Ṣayyād (or Ibn Ṣāʾid) of the well-known reports, but the personal name given here is unusual. The source's form has been kept rather than corrected, per style guide §11.

flags.context: والسحر … فهذا يحصل به خرق للعادة وهو للشر فهو كفر بصاحبه
options: it is unbelief on the part of the one who does it
it renders the one who practises it an unbeliever
it amounts to unbelief in its practitioner
flags.note: A ruling of takfīr on the practice of sorcery, stated here in a single clause with no qualification and no discussion of the conditions the jurists attach to it. It has been rendered exactly as given, neither softened nor extended. Note for the reviewer that the Sheikh refers back to a definition of sorcery given elsewhere ('what has already been defined, in its two kinds'), which is not on this page.

translator_notes: Hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The Sheikh refers back to an earlier definition of sorcery ('what has already been defined, in its two kinds') which is not present on this page; the cross-reference has been kept and nothing has been supplied for it.
He attributes the exchange with Saf ibn Sayyad to 'the Ṣaḥīḥ' without naming which, and gives no grading for the report about Musaylimah or for the sayings of al-Junayd. No grading has been supplied.
The seven-fold division is the Sheikh's framing of what 'the scholars' say; he does not name them, and no attribution has been added.
Source slip preserved verbatim in body_ar: فيها كلمة واحدة صدق وتسعة وتسعون كذبة, where the numeral agreement shifts between the two halves of the same sentence (تسعا وتسعين then تسعة وتسعون).
